correction.text: "along the coast of Newfoundland, the Canadian Maritimes and northern New England"; "Maritime Archaic sites have been found as far south as Maine and as far north as Labrador"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "The Maritime Archaic began in approximately 7000 BC and lasted until approximately 3500 BC"; the dossier starts at the project floor. Drawn as Newfoundland, Labrador, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island and Maine (2,165 land cells, about 550,000 km2): the people were coastal sea-mammal hunters, so the whole provinces overstate the land and the interior of Labrador was not theirs. The page has no infobox and gives no area.

region.text: "along the coast of Newfoundland, the Canadian Maritimes and northern New England"; "Maritime Archaic sites have been found as far south as Maine and as far north as Labrador"

ledger.note: 6000 BCE (project floor): the Maritime Archaic sea-mammal hunters already work the coasts from Labrador to Maine. "The Maritime Archaic began in approximately 7000 BC and lasted until approximately 3500 BC"; "The culture consisted of sea-mammal hunters in the subarctic who used wooden boats." The culture begins before the floor; the provinces named for "the coast of Newfoundland, the Canadian Maritimes and northern New England" are the dossier's reading.

region.text: "along the coast of Newfoundland, the Canadian Maritimes and northern New England"; "Maritime Archaic sites have been found as far south as Maine and as far north as Labrador"

ledger.note: 3500 BCE: the Maritime Archaic ends. "lasted until approximately 3500 BC"; the page links the end to the arrival of Paleo-Eskimo groups that may have competed with them for resources (a claim marked citation needed), and says the Red Ochre burials of the northeastern United States may represent the culture's final phases (scholars still debate this); the land is therefore left to nobody, as no page opened names a successor with a dossier.

certainty.note: A coastal culture with no recorded border; the extent follows the northernmost and southernmost sites the page names.

sources.title: Maritime Archaic
sources.note: Dates (about 7000 BC to about 3500 BC), extent (Newfoundland, the Maritimes, northern New England; Labrador to Maine), Paleo-Eskimo and Red Ochre.

notes: Maritime Archaic, Atlantic Canada and Maine. One page opened. The page has no infobox; dates and extent are from the body. The extent is whole provinces for a coastal culture (overstated, especially interior Labrador and Nova Scotia). The Paleo-Eskimo groups said to have followed have no dossier in this batch (Arctic Small Tool tradition starts c. 2500 BCE on the Archaic page).
